title: Add Chrome extension RAG quickstart with offline index and synced tool-calls
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Add a browser-extension quickstart demonstrating offline IndexedDB indexing, optional cloud-sync to Redwood Private, and a pattern for syncing tool-calls from extension background to a hosted Redwood tool runtime. Useful for edge/offline agents and mobile-light clients.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a new quickstart that demonstrates embedding-based RAG inside a Chrome extension with (1) an offline IndexedDB-backed indexer, (2) a small background worker that batches and syncs new documents to an optional Redwood Private sync endpoint, and (3) an example of reliably forwarding tool-calls (open-in-tab, search, and external API proxies) from the extension to a trusted tool runtime.

Motivation: We have many requests for lighter-weight client-side RAG experiences and reproducible examples for browser-based agents that need to work offline or with intermittent connectivity. This quickstart shows one pragmatic pattern: keep a local index for immediate recall/latency, emit telemetry and async sync to server-side storage for durability and cross-device replay, and handle tool-calls via a verified background channel to avoid leaking user tokens.

What changed (high level):
- New quickstart folder quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/ with README, manifest, background worker, popup UI, IndexedDB indexer, and a small local test harness.
- New docs page docs/contributing/extension-guidelines.md that outlines security considerations for browser extensions (token handling, CSP, permission scoping).
- Add a lightweight node helper server in quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/proxy-server/ (optional) that demonstrates a recommended pattern to host tool runtimes behind a short-lived signed session token.
- Tests and Playwright-based smoke runner in .github/workflows/quickstart-chrome.yml to validate build and basic flows in CI.

Usage and testing:
- Follow quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/README.md to load the unpacked extension in Chrome (dev). The README includes a one-command flow to run the local proxy and seed an index.
- The extension exposes an "index page" where you can drag text/files to index; it will generate embeddings (using your Redwood API key from environment) and store them in IndexedDB.
- When offline, the extension searches the local index and renders results. When connectivity is restored, it batches unsynced items and posts to the proxy server or Redwood Private sync endpoint.
- Tool-calls (for example, openUrl and runSearch) are routed to the background worker which will either run locally (open tab) or forward to the proxy-server endpoint using a short-lived ephemeral token.

Security notes:
- The quickstart README and docs/contributing/extension-guidelines.md explicitly show how to avoid storing long-lived API keys in localStorage and how to delegate to a backend to sign ephemeral tokens.
- We recommend using Redwood Private for production sync; the proxy server is intentionally minimal and documented as NOT production-ready.

Small illustrative snippet (from indexeddb.ts) included inline in README for clarity: const db = await openDB('redwood-extension', 1); await db.put('docs', { id: id, text: text, embedding: embedding });

Review conversation (selected):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Nice pattern — can we avoid storing embeddings in plain IndexedDB if the extension is marked for public distribution? Suggest an opt-in encrypted store and clarify in docs."
- Priya Menon (author): "Agreed; added a section in extension-guidelines.md describing an optional IndexedDB encryption shim using Web Crypto API and a template for prompting the user to enable encryption."
- Xiaoyu Zhang (reviewer): "CI smoke run failed on first attempt due to Playwright connecting to headless Chrome in CI image. Recommend switching to ubuntu-latest and adding xvfb in workflow."
- Priya: "Fixed: updated workflow to use the official Playwright action which sets up the browsers; also added retries for the smoke check."
- Marisol Reyes (reviewer): "Can you add a quick note about long-running syncs causing battery drain and a recommended throttle?"
- Priya: "Added throttle settings to README and the proxy-server example (batch size 32, delay 5s default)."

CI status and runs:
- .github/workflows/quickstart-chrome.yml: ran 3 times; first run failed (Playwright launch), second passed after workflow change, third is a re-run tied to approval.
- Checks: build: pass; smoke-playwright: pass; lint: pass; docs-linkcheck: pass

Merge notes:
- Approvals: Liam O'Connor approved, Xiaoyu Zhang approved after requested changes were addressed.
- Merge method: squash (squash merge commit used).
- Post-merge tasks: added a quickstart entry to the docs site navigation and scheduled a follow-up to add a reproducible e2e harness (ENG-1432).

Related: Linear ENG-1432 (browser quickstarts initiative), PM-321 (quickstarts backlog).

Known limitations & follow-ups:
- Not intended as a hardened production extension; proxy-server is for demos only.
- We should add an optional encrypted sync layer (follow-up ticket ENG-1500).
- Add more robust Playwright tests covering offline->sync transition (follow-up ENG-1551).
